event_text: An influx was registered by high gas readings at surface while circulating bottoms up from TD at 3400 m, with a gas peak of 52.3% before the well was shut in.
At 2329 m a 900 litres gain was recorded, indicating a kick was taking place and the drilling was suspended due to a well control situation.
notes: sidetrack relates to the later stuck pipe, not the kick

event_text: The MWD data records from 3070 m to TD are missing, due to washout, lost signal, stuck pipe and MWD tool lost in hole.
While drilling salt at 2780 m pipe stuck, and when attempting to pull free collars parted.
Minor shallow gas peaks were observed from mud gas readings in the pilot hole below the 30" casing at 498 - 500 m.
Core 1 was a "junk core".
notes: 'junk core' is a core type, not a fishing event

event_text: The drill pipe became stuck at 486 m and the hole was abandoned with the top of fish at 323 m.
The pipe got stuck at 1572 m.
A dive was made to determine if the fish was on the ocean floor.
34.5% of the total rig time was lost time due to fishing, waiting on weather, waiting for replacement of equipment, and hole problems.
Severe hole problems with tight spots and repeated fall-out of large quantities of cavings were experienced in the bottom 12 1/4" section of the well.
Jarring did not free the pipe, and a cement plug was set above the fish.
When coring for core no 10 the core jammed at 2512.5 m and the core head matrix was left in the hole.
The relative overpressure in the ORELN2 Formations is around 30 Bar.
notes: formation pressure statement, not a drilling episode

event_text: Apart from stuck conductor in the top hole, requiring a re-spud, there were no significant problems encountered in the operations.
Pumping lost circulation material, without changing the mud weight, stopped loss of mud at 1710 m.
While drilling the 36" hole at 167 m, the drill string stuck.
This resulted in a total loss of 28 days.
notes: 'total loss of 28 days' = lost rig time, not lost circulation

event_text: Boulders were encountered between 380 m and 400 m, but created no torquing problems while drilling.
Below this level background gas varied between 1 - 15 % with trip gas up to 32%.
The first sidetrack was kicked off at 314 m after unsuccessful fishing (lost hole opener).
During controlling of the kick, a large proportion of gas was vented and light low gravity yellowish oil recovered from the mud.
These were: dropped 10-3/4" casing, failed wellhead, well control incident, failure of the HPC tieback packer and waiting on weather.
When trying to back off the drill pipe twisted off, leaving a 340 m fish in the hole.

Due to concerns of further severe losses, the technical sidetrack was not drilled to a sufficient depth to penetrate the expected FWL, however, wireline pressures, fluid gradients and samples were acquired in the gas and oil zones suggesting a GOC at 1912.5 m (1910 m TVD).
The well was shut in and several attempts were made to gain control, without success.
notes: developed into an underground blow out

event_text: Losses of 26 bbl/hr were noted at 5475 m and were cured after pumping and soaking 2 LCM pills.
At 2963 m the drill pipe stuck in salt, and after five days of unsuccessful fishing operations, it was decided to abandon the hole.
The drill string got stuck twice, backed off, and after unsuccessful fishing, technical sidetracks were performed.
notes: outcome phrase precedes the fishing trigger

event_text: Boulders were experienced in the interval 155 -170 m MD and some time was spent to correct the inclination.
